bridges.description: Craig's generic theistic routes combine with resurrection to reach the Christian God revealed in Jesus.
Philosophical and scientific considerations support a finite past and cosmic beginning.
A beginning of space-time requires and conceptually identifies a personal transcendent cause.
Life-permitting fine-tuning is best explained by design after necessity and chance are rejected.
Objective moral truth is experientially known and grounded in God's necessary nature.
Historical facts, religious context and comparative uniqueness support resurrection as vindication of Jesus.
Immediate religious experience supplies defeasible personal warrant apart from argument.
Craig's offered reasons may fail to establish the motion without Pyle proving that God does not exist.
Neither a beginning argument nor a cause label by itself warrants a timeless personal transcendent God.
Fine-tuning probability assumptions and the comparative content of design remain underdetermined.
Secular moral truth-makers remain available and divine command faces an autonomy challenge.
Source transmission, alternative explanations and belief formation weaken the historical resurrection inference.
Comparative reports and false-positive rates limit testimonial support for miracles.
Religious diversity requires a criterion distinguishing accurate from mistaken experiences.

sections.title: Whether the universe began
sections.rationale: This section isolates the philosophical and scientific beginning premise that must hold before Craig's causal inference can operate.

sections.title: From a cosmic cause to a personal creator
sections.rationale: This section tests both the deduction of a cause and the disputed further identification of that cause as timeless, personal and transcendent.

sections.title: Fine-tuning, probability and design
sections.rationale: This independent theistic route turns on probability-space assumptions, multiverse alternatives and whether design has comparative explanatory support.

sections.title: Moral truth and its foundation
sections.rationale: This independent route concerns whether moral truths exist, how they are known, and whether secular or divine accounts can ground them.

sections.title: Historical resurrection and Christian identification
sections.rationale: This is Craig's main bridge from generic monotheism to the specifically Christian God and includes source reliability, historical alternatives and Jewish context.

sections.title: Comparative miracles and testimonial standards
sections.rationale: This section tests the evidential policy applied to miracle reports through Ganesh, naturalist track record, Humean updating and a stated positive evidence threshold.

sections.title: Critical burden, cumulative scope and religious experience
sections.rationale: This section preserves Pyle's limited critical posture, Craig's noninferential experience claim and the final clarification of how Craig reaches the exact Christian motion.
